solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Crucial moment of stomach workout? (6,4)

blocks.note: the setter's reading: an everyday phrase for the decisive point when pressure peaks
the surface's reading: the slot in a gym session given to a sit-up-like exercise for the abdominal muscles

annotation.surface: A gym instructor announcing the dreaded ab section of the class.
annotation.walkthrough: A crunch is a sit-up-like exercise for the stomach muscles, so the question mark invites a literal reading of an everyday phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Crunch time is the critical point when a decision or effort must be made.

entries.clue: Prickly types caught opening of play (5)

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Awkward, spiky people spotted at the start of a theatre show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening of play' looks like a first-letter instruction for P; here it is the whole first act, ACT I.
annotation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny plants, so prickly types in a playful sense.

entries.clue: Put ethane in a new configuration to add more risk (2,3,4)

indicators.note: the letters of PUT ETHANE are arranged differently

annotation.surface: A chemist rearranging a molecule in a more dangerous way.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry vocabulary hides a poker phrase: the ante is the stake each player puts in before the deal.
annotation.definitionFit: To up the ante is to raise the stakes, increasing what is at risk.

entries.clue: Islanders check out novel writer (7,7)

indicators.note: out = wrong, not in order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Residents of an island leave their hotel after trying a new author.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check out' reads as one phrasal verb; split it, so 'check' is fodder and 'out' the indicator. 'Novel' is also a pun: a writer of novels, not a new one.
annotation.definitionFit: Dickens wrote novels such as Oliver Twist and Great Expectations.

entries.clue: Sweet Edward posted to followers (7)

blocks.note: Ted is a short form of Edward

annotation.surface: A charming man named Edward is sent off to join his devotees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Posted' pretends Edward was sent somewhere; it is social-media posting.
annotation.definitionFit: To tweet is to post a message to one's followers on Twitter.

entries.clue: Back worker to assemble bulk of money? (7)

indicators.note: most of the word, dropping its last letter

annotation.surface: A worker who backs a scheme to gather a pile of cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back worker' reads like a supporter or a behind-the-scenes employee; it is someone who works on people's backs.
annotation.definitionFit: A masseur kneads muscles, often of the back.

entries.clue: Seize boat that’s docked in reverse (4)

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter goes
the remaining letters run backwards

blocks.note: BARGE with its last letter docked

annotation.surface: Pirates commandeering a vessel that has backed into its berth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Docked' suggests a boat tied up in harbour, which fits the surface perfectly; here it means cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to grab something is to take hold of it suddenly, just as to seize it is.

entries.clue: Right, what was that muscle treatment programme? (5)

annotation.surface: A patient asking the physio to repeat the name of the exercise plan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Muscle treatment' looks like one phrase; 'muscle' belongs to the wordplay and the definition is just 'treatment programme'.
annotation.definitionFit: Rehab is a programme of rehabilitation, for injury or addiction.

entries.clue: Boy secures lines on trees for film industry (9)

indicators.note: to secure is to hold something safely, so BOY holds LL safe inside it
in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: l = line, doubled for the plural
a wood is a group of trees

annotation.surface: A lad tying ropes onto trees, perhaps building a treehouse.
annotation.walkthrough: BO(LL)Y then WOOD: Bollywood is the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai.
annotation.definitionFit: Bollywood is India's Mumbai-based film industry.

entries.clue: Present lady’s leg? (8,6)

blocks.note: literally, what fills a lady's stocking

annotation.surface: An odd gift suggestion, or an innuendo about a woman's leg.
annotation.walkthrough: A stocking filler is a small present put in a Christmas stocking; the question mark flags the literal second reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Stocking fillers are the little gifts that go into a Christmas stocking.

entries.clue: Construction of bars seen around extravagant home (7)

indicators.note: CAGE is placed around OTT

blocks.note: a cage is built of bars; the outer piece

annotation.surface: A jail built around a showy mansion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs or a prison; 'construction of bars' is a thing built from them. OTT, short for over the top, is standard crossword shorthand for extravagant.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cottage is one kind of small country dwelling, and the clue's plain 'home' covers it.

entries.clue: Was on the bench, say, with team lacking water carrier? (7)

indicators.note: the team's name is missing SEA

blocks.note: sat = was seated, on a bench for example

annotation.surface: A substitute footballer whose team has no water boy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was on the bench' suggests a substitute; 'say' warns it only exemplifies sitting. Chelsea is a London football club.
annotation.definitionFit: A satchel is a bag for carrying books.

entries.clue: Time taken up by mixing delicate drink (4,5)

indicators.note: T is absorbed into the rearranged letters
the letters of DELICATE are stirred into a new order

annotation.surface: A bartender spending ages making a dainty cocktail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delicate drink' looks like one phrase; 'delicate' is fodder and the definition is just 'drink'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a latte served over ice is one specific coffee-shop beverage, and 'drink' is its broad category.

entries.clue: Grumpy after end of director’s cut for Taxi Driver (5)

indicators.note: the letter is removed from CRABBY

blocks.note: last letter of director, cut from CRABBY

annotation.surface: A bad-tempered reaction to the director's cut of the Scorsese film Taxi Driver.
annotation.walkthrough: The film title and 'director's cut' make it all cinema; the capitalised Taxi Driver is simply a cab driver.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cabby is an informal word for the person driving a cab, stripped of the film title's capitals.

entries.clue: Over Tannoy, makes illegal announcement about match (5)

indicators.note: a Tannoy is a public-address system, so the word is heard, not seen

annotation.surface: A stadium loudspeaker declaring something forbidden at a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests sport and the Tannoy a stadium; the match is a marriage. Banns are the church announcement of an intended wedding.
annotation.definitionFit: Banns are read out in church to announce a forthcoming marriage.

entries.clue: Bishop doesn’t have pale or dark pen, perhaps? (5,4)

annotation.surface: A bishop choosing between a pale and a dark pen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool; a pen is a female swan, so a dark one might be a black swan.
annotation.definitionFit: A female black swan is a dark pen; 'perhaps' because a black swan need not be female.

entries.clue: Exploits Democrat blundering before event (7-2)

blocks.note: a do = a party or event

annotation.surface: A Democratic politician taking advantage of the chance to gaffe before a function.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' reads as a verb; it is the noun, daring deeds.
annotation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic, daring action, the stuff of exploits.

entries.clue: Cries of surprise reach a climax after grand technical jargon (9)

indicators.note: the cries and the climax come after grand, so G is sent to the front ahead of them

blocks.note: G = grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
eek! is a squeal of alarm
to peak = to reach the highest point

annotation.surface: Gasps of amazement building to a crescendo over some grand technical language.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After grand' puts G first, ahead of the two pieces that precede it in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Geekspeak is the jargon of computer enthusiasts and technical experts.

entries.clue: States things in a camera incorrectly? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: Someone mis-describing what is inside a camera.
annotation.walkthrough: 'States' reads as a verb; it is the United States, so 'States things' are American artefacts.
annotation.definitionFit: Americana are objects and lore characteristic of American culture.

entries.clue: Fixed radar on small European country (7)

indicators.note: fixed = mended, reassembled into a new order

annotation.surface: A radar trained on a tiny nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fixed radar' reads as a stationary radar set; 'fixed' is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the tiny Pyrenean principality between France and Spain is one of Europe's microstates.

entries.clue: Pass with two good marks and a bad one (7)

blocks.note: A and B, two good grades
a stain is a bad mark

annotation.surface: A student passing an exam with two good grades and one poor one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass' suggests passing an exam; it is passing on a vote.
annotation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to vote or take part, to pass.

entries.clue: Said yes, ignoring a deadly sin (5)

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out of account, so the A is disregarded and dropped

annotation.surface: Someone who consented while turning a blind eye to sin.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface as an article; the first one is the letter to remove.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: avarice sits in the traditional list of seven, beside pride, lust and sloth.

entries.clue: Period spent in strike? (5)

blocks.note: cricket slang for an innings, the stint a batsman spends 'in' at the crease
strike as a verb: to hit or rap

annotation.surface: Time served during an industrial stoppage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout. In cricket a batsman is 'in' while batting, and a knock is an innings.
annotation.definitionFit: A knock is a batsman's innings in cricket, and to knock is to strike.

entries.clue: Tour regularly has scrap round route (5)

indicators.note: take every other letter of tour

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of tOuR

annotation.surface: A tour bus routinely gets into a fight on a circular route.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a fight; it is a small piece.
annotation.definitionFit: An orbit is a circular path around something, a round route.

entries.clue: Detectives lost out (9)

annotation.surface: Police officers who failed to get something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lost out' reads as one phrase; 'out' is the definition, as a cricketer is out when dismissed.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricket sense: when the umpire's finger goes up, the batsman's innings is over and he walks off, sent away by the fielding side.

entries.clue: Possibly does without roof of tower block (5)

indicators.note: does is one example of deer
without = outside, so DEER goes around T
the top letter of tower, in a down clue

blocks.note: does, female deer, are possibly deer; the outer piece
roof of tower, its first letter

annotation.surface: An instruction about a tower block that has no roof.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' is the plural of doe, not the verb, and 'without' means outside. 'Tower block' is one phrase in the surface but splits here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: discouraging someone from acting, by fear or doubt, blocks what they meant to do.

entries.clue: Refuse place in sport workshop (7)

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so BIN is put in the middle of WEAR

blocks.note: to sport = to wear, as clothing; the outer piece
a bin is where refuse goes

annotation.surface: Turning down a spot in a sports workshop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb; it is rubbish, and 'sport' is the verb to wear.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a web-based seminar is a training session held online, a modern kind of workshop.

entries.clue: Delivered beer intended for infirmity (7)

indicators.note: delivered as a speech is, so the sound counts

annotation.surface: A beer delivery meant for a sick person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a drinks delivery; it means spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a bodily weakness or complaint, usually a minor or lingering one.

entries.clue: Star returns seizing time for snack (4)

indicators.note: SUN is turned back to NUS
to seize is to grab and hold, so NUS clasps T within it

annotation.surface: A celebrity comes back to grab a bite.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity; it is the Sun, reversed and wrapped round T: NU(T)S.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: peanuts, cashews and almonds are the classic bar nibbles, one kind of snack.

entries.clue: Queen, potentially, with even less money for merchant? (10)

blocks.note: in chess, a pawn reaching the far rank can become a queen
broker = more broke, with even less money

annotation.surface: A monarch, possibly even poorer, turning to trade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty; it is the chess piece a pawn may be promoted to. BROKER is read as the comparative of broke.
annotation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker is a dealer who lends money against goods.
